blocks.text: Greengold offers operating-system-level native threads (`std.thread`). `Thread.spawn(f)` starts a function in the background, `join()` waits for it to finish. To pass a parameter there is `spawn_with_param(f, value)`. None of them needs `unsafe`.

code: print("worker A running in a background thread")

blocks.text: `Thread`, `Mutex`, `Cond` and channels are **operating system objects: they are moved, not copied**. Writing `n = m` moves `m`; a second, independent lock is not made. `m.clone()` does not compile (GG0323). To hand a lock or a channel to another function you use a `read`/`lend` parameter.

blocks.q: Which method waits for a thread to finish?
blocks.why: `join()` waits until the thread has finished.
Operating system objects are not copied; a copy would mean two separate locks.
